spec: 3DS (Autodesk 3D Studio chunk format, as lib3ds documents it): a real file, an object node whose parent is a camera's node: its keys are in the frame the camera aims (at its target's node, Z up, looking down -Z)
source: assimp/assimp at 711b4e9bbde2, test/models/3DS/CameraRollAnimWithChildObject.3ds (BSD-3-Clause, see ../LICENSE-assimp); expectations read from the file by tools/corpus/tds.py: its vertices' bounds and area, each box's place from its mesh matrix's origin, and keys as its tracks have them. The generator checks that the camera's look-at frame (from its position and its target's, no roll on frame 0) times Box02's first position and rotation keys is Box02's mesh matrix, to 1e-4. The file doesn't say which way a roll turns (it is 0 where the file was saved), so nothing that depends on the roll is compared. A target's node is named as 3ds Max names it, `<camera>.Target`
